name: Let it bounce at the wall
summary: Alone at a wall, play each serve-and-return pattern with the bounces the two-bounce rule asks for and count early volleys as own faults.
setup: Tape a line on the wall about 0.9 m above the floor (the net) and a floor line about 6 m from the wall
Serve against the wall from behind the floor line; the rebound is the return: let it bounce, then play a soft third shot above the line
Let the next rebound bounce too, then you may volley or play off the bounce
Count an own fault each time you volley a ball that had to bounce (the first two rebounds) or the ball goes below the line. Sets of 10 patterns
success_criterion: In each of 3 sets of 10 patterns, at most 1 own fault
safety_notes: Soft pace. Let rebounds come to you; do not lunge or run for them. Stop if in pain.
coach_rationale: (judgment) Volleying a ball that had to bounce is an own fault that ends rallies (the AN-07 fault share); rehearsing the serve, bounce, bounce rhythm alone builds the habit of waiting. A wall gives many repetitions with no partner. The fault rules are UNVERIFIED in this app (P7): count them as your rules allow. Unverified coaching content until a human coach reviews the library (P15).
